findings.title: Scope matches the slice plan entry, and the deferrals are licensed by it
findings.description: Plan entry 25 asks for Part A (record what was injected against what existed, in frontmatter + findings header + `--output json`, on both paths), Part B (a truncated, unread diff is not a clean PASS, design picks between CONCERNS and failing), and Part C (record the answering model, decide what counts as "differs"). The design delivers exactly those three, and every item it drops is explicitly permitted: the plan says diff ordering and `--stat` are "in scope only if design shows it is small; otherwise it becomes an issue", and D7 defers them to #137 with a substantive reason (ordering needs a per-template "what counts as source" policy — a decision, not plumbing). `max_file_size_bytes` defaults and #114 are excluded as the plan requires. The two files the plan's Part A did not anticipate (the total-injection-limit path, #138's file-body truncation) are handled by scoping the second out rather than absorbing it.

findings.title: `aiModel` can name a model that did not write the review
findings.description: D12 states "`aiModel` is the **last** model reported, the one that wrote the review", and the Data Flow repeats `result.model = last answering model`. But State Management specifies `TurnCapture` accumulation as "answering models append in order, deduplicated", and D8 has the providers stamping `metadata["answering_models"]` as a "distinct, first-seen order" list. Those two rules disagree about what "last" means. For the sequence turn 1 = `[A, B]` (possible within the agentic loop, per D8's "Accumulate distinct values across the agentic loop") followed by the #92 recovery turn reporting `A`, dedup yields `[A, B]`, whose last element is `B` — a model that did not produce the persisted review. The design must state the rule explicitly: either `result.model` is the last model reported *per call* (independent of the deduped list used for the digest), or the list preserves last-occurrence order. As written, the one fact this slice exists to record can be wrong in exactly the multi-turn case D12 was added to handle.

findings.title: The coverage cap silently discards 919's `derived` verdict provenance
findings.description: D5 says "Only `impose_diff_coverage` sets it", but `VerdictSource.DERIVED` is already set by `_verdict_from_findings` when the summary parse failed and the verdict was recovered from finding severities (verified in `parsers.py:993`). Both conditions can hold simultaneously: the cap fires on a `PASS` with a truncated diff and zero successful tool calls, and a *derived* PASS is precisely the shape where no summary verdict was parsed — 919 Part B exists because that derived PASS auto-clears a gate that reads frontmatter. When the cap applies, the artifact's single `verdictSource` slot is overwritten from `derived` to `imposed`, so the #97 signal ("the model never said this") is destroyed at the moment it is most needed, and nothing else in the artifact records it. The design needs a stated precedence and a home for the displaced fact — either `imposed` subsumes `derived` and the digest says so, or the two are separate keys.

findings.title: The synthetic finding omits `location:`, departing from the 904 convention it bypasses
findings.description: D4 states "It has no `location` because it cites no file. `location_verified` stays `None`." The slice plan's entry 3 (904) requires `location:` on *every* finding, PASS included, and establishes `unverified` as "the explicit 'I don't know' token", with `parsers.py` normalizing missing/blank/`-`/`global` to `unverified`. Because the synthetic finding is constructed in `impose_diff_coverage` rather than parsed, that normalization never runs, so the artifact carries a finding with no location — the one shape the convention forbids, and a fourth state for any consumer (904 records ensemble merged-finding dedup as keying on location). "Cites no file" is exactly what `unverified` means; the fix is one word, and the design should say why it did not use it.

findings.title: The synthetic finding's remedy names the wrong knob for the total-limit case
findings.description: D3 deliberately records the `_add_injection` skip as the same fact as a `_truncate` cut (`total_chars=len(diff)`, `injected_chars=0`), and D4's rule fires on `truncated`, which D1 defines as `injected_chars < total_chars` — so the total-limit case produces the synthetic finding. But D4's template hardcodes the remedy "Raise `review.max_file_size_bytes`" and the sentence "the first 256000 reached the model (review.max_file_size_bytes)". In the D3 case nothing reached the model and `max_file_size_bytes` was not the binding constraint, so the artifact tells the operator to raise a limit that will change nothing. This is the artifact's only actionable output on that path, and the design treats the two causes as "the same fact, not a different fact" without noting that the *remedy* is not the same. Render the sentence from which limit bound (the counts are already carried), or word it cause-neutrally.

findings.title: A new module for one predicate, next to the module that already owns model ids
findings.description: `models/snapshot.py` is introduced to hold `answers_as_requested`, described as living "next to `models/aliases.py` because it is about model ids, not reviews." `aliases.py` is already the module about model ids (`resolve_model_alias`, `model_allows_tools`) and has no dependency that this predicate would violate. A one-predicate, regex-only file is the lighter option's heavier sibling; fold it in unless a second consumer is already foreseen, and if it does need its own module, name it for the rule (`model_identity.py`) rather than for one of its three accepted shapes.

findings.title: Expanding `VerdictSource` needs the vocabulary contract updated, and the "no external reader" evidence is grep-only
findings.description: The `VerdictSource` docstring in `review/models.py` documents "a closed two-value vocabulary (D7)", and the design's argument (the concern was open reason strings, not member count) is fair but is not the same as the docstring saying so — the component table lists the enum change without listing the docstring/contract update. Separately, D5 rests on "grep of context-forge on 20260926 found no reader" and the Integration Points section calls the change "All additive", but 919 Part B chose the frontmatter key specifically so Context Forge could switch on it without squadron dictating policy; a third value is a value change to a key another repository may now branch on, not an addition. I could not verify CF's current state (external repo, unverified), so this is a note to re-confirm rather than an assertion that a reader exists.
